scope: The model separates send permission, provider effect, reply save, takeover, retry choice, and publication.
Each permit can reach the provider once, before or after takeover. It can also remain undelivered in any trace prefix.
Each provider effect returns one of two reply values. The reply can be delayed or left unsaved.
P3 counts locally admitted send permits, not arbitrary provider effects. P5 checks the selected attempt when publication occurs, not only at the end.
The provider is honest. In the proposed model, a single admitted invocation has one reply value; conflicting provider replies are not part of that model.
P4 is checked on reachable edges under honest replies. Result replacement is refused by construction; this study has no P4 guard-removal experiment.
A known result is saved only by the owner of that invocation. Saving evidence is separate from current publication.
The search checks every generated edge. Equal replay and refused commands leave state unchanged and are omitted.
Breadth-first traversal makes each reported trace shortest in state-changing model steps for that failed property.
observations.search: breadth-first search of all reachable states within finite bounds

This is a finite abstract model. It does not run OpenBot or test database locks, network loss, or real threads.
The search does not test pause, recovery, or fencing. Fencing means refusing a write from an old work owner.
The search has one child handoff and at most one added correction or child. It is not a proof for unbounded task trees.

semantics: Each action ID occurs once. All orders are attempted; an action with unmet order rules is a no-op.
Pause, active-work, and terminal-record flags stay in a state that permits closure. Input use stands for an activation that has ended.
The child owes result-1 at the start. The close oracle checks live open children and all required input IDs.
Read obligations saves w and the open-child test. Read context then saves v and the pending-input test.
Commit tests the saved facts and the enabled version guards. It does not repeat the live oracle.
Accept and input use change v. Retire and child creation change w. The child result is accepted before safe retirement.
An accepted correction is an added required input. A new child adds both an open obligation and a required result.
Closure freezes this round. Later attempted actions are no-ops; a real later input would need a new round.
A successful close means the commit took effect. The separate true and false counts say whether that close was sound.

observations: All 400 ordered role lists and 736 grouped variants passed the leaf oracle.
All 1472 model and action traces matched; 920 blocked traces had no dispatch.
All 32 build and release failure cases tried every owned release in reverse order.
Right replacement kept its handler. Wrong precedence and a shared handler key stopped both model and action steps before dispatch.
The weak prompt count check accepted 2 messages after the restriction was lost.
Two hooks each passed local idempotence, but their chain changed (0, 0) to (0, 1) to (1, 1).
Per-hook receipts kept the chain at (0, 1), with 2 receipts, after prefix and full replay.
Across 30 seeds and 213 write attempts, each key had 1 committed write.
Extended cases checked 847 lists and 3182 traces with repeats, empty records, several tools, and all groupings.
All 1,681 ordered pairs of idempotent four-state maps were checked: 601 commuted, 264 had a non-idempotent chain, and 816 had an idempotent chain without commuting.
All 124 completed scope cases kept every exit cause; 3 blocked cases stayed closing.
All 4166 finalizer dependency graphs through four resources matched the independent live-resource oracle.
Two instances sharing a receipt key lost one intended write; stable instance keys kept both writes once.
Six single-rule ablations each exposed one designed fault. The full rule set avoided those faults and accepted all six safe controls.
